Example 3 (condition)

Example 4 (request)

Example 5 (fact)
- Original: "The [price] of the item is [lower] than last year."

- Alternative natural phrasing: "The price of the item is not lower than last year" or "The price of the item is not the same as last year" depending on intended emphasis.

Notes for reproducibility
- To negate a bracketed segment, replace the enclosed phrase with its logical negation, while keeping the rest of the sentence structure intact.
- When the bracketed segment is a verb phrase (e.g., [spend], [send]), the negation often involves adding not or choosing a semantically opposite action (avoid, refrain from, not want to, etc.) to produce a natural-sounding sentence.
- When the bracketed segment is a noun or adjective (e.g., [price], [best way]), negate with a corresponding negative predicate (not, cannot, unlikely, etc.) while preserving grammatical correctness.
